title_en: The War with My Alarm Clock
description_ru: Юмористический рассказ о человеке, который ненавидит утро и пробует всё новые способы просыпаться вовремя.
text:
I am not a morning person. In fact, I think that morning is a mistake. The world should start at eleven o'clock, with a warm drink and a long, silent walk to the kitchen. Unfortunately, my job starts at eight, and for years I have been fighting a war with my alarm clock. I want to tell you about the funniest battle in this war.

It began last winter, when I realised that I was late for work three times in one week. My boss, Mrs Gray, is a kind woman, but she has a very cold look. She said, "If this happens again, we are going to have a serious conversation." I went home and made a plan. I decided to buy the loudest alarm clock in the shop. I wanted something that could wake up a whole street.

The shop assistant showed me a clock with two big bells on the top. "This one is used by people who sleep like stones," he said. It cost fifteen pounds, and it looked like something from a hundred years ago. I put it next to my bed and set it for six thirty. That night I went to sleep with a smile. I felt like a person who had solved all of his problems.

At six thirty, the clock exploded with noise. It sounded like a fire engine inside my head. I jumped out of bed and hit the clock, and it flew across the room and landed under the wardrobe. It kept ringing there. I could not reach it, so I lay on the floor with my arm under the wardrobe for five minutes. Then the clock stopped, and I felt very proud. But I had also woken up my neighbours. When I went outside, the old man from the next flat was standing in front of his door in his pyjamas. "Was that an earthquake?" he asked.

The next morning, I was so tired that I fell asleep again at breakfast. I decided that the clock was too loud, and the problem was not the sound, but my brain. It learned to ignore the noise. So I tried a new idea. I put the clock on the other side of the room, so that I had to get out of bed to switch it off. It worked for two days. On the third day, I got up, turned off the clock, and went straight back to bed. I do not remember doing this. I only remember waking up at ten o'clock with a terrible headache.

My sister, who is a very organised person, told me to use my phone. "There are many applications for people like you," she said. I found one that is called "Wake Up Challenge". To turn off the alarm, you have to solve a difficult maths problem. I was sure that it would help. But at six thirty in the morning, my brain does not know how to add seven and eight. I looked at the phone for ten minutes, and the alarm was ringing all the time. In the end, I threw the phone onto the sofa, and it kept screaming from there.

I tried other things, too. I bought a clock that jumps off the table and runs around the room. It was funny for the first day, but then it ran under the bed and I could not find it. I tried a light that gets brighter slowly, like the sun. I woke up, but I was angry that the sun was fake. I even asked my neighbour to knock on my door at seven o'clock. He did it twice, and then he asked me to pay him.

Finally, my sister gave me the best advice. "Go to bed earlier," she said. At first, I laughed. Going to bed earlier is a great idea in theory, but in the evening I always find something more interesting to do. I watch a film, read a book or look at the internet. "Just try for one week," she begged. So I did. I turned off my computer at ten o'clock and was asleep by half past ten.

The next morning, a miracle happened. I woke up before the alarm, and I felt good. I made breakfast, looked out of the window and arrived at work ten minutes early. Mrs Gray was surprised and gave me a cup of coffee. Now I use a simple, quiet clock, and I go to bed early. Only one thing has not changed. I still believe that morning is a mistake.

questions.question: Why did the writer buy a loud alarm clock?
questions.answer: He was late for work three times in one week and his boss warned him.

questions.question: What happened with the first alarm clock?
questions.answer: It was so loud that it woke the neighbours, and the old man asked about an earthquake.

questions.question: What was the problem with the maths application?
questions.answer: At 6:30 his brain could not solve the problem, so the alarm kept ringing.
